summary: Pluggable credential storage: SecretStore protocol (runtime-checkable) and FilesystemStore implementation. Domain-namespaced YAML files with 0o600 permissions, tombstone-based clear tracking, and fcntl file locking for concurrent refresh safety.

key_classes.name: SecretStore
key_classes.summary: Runtime-checkable Protocol. Methods: load, save, clear, is_cleared, list_users, lock. Domain/provider/user key space.

key_classes.name: FilesystemStore
key_classes.summary: YAML-backed implementation. Layout: base_dir/{domain}/{provider}-{user}.yaml. Atomic writes via temp file + os.replace. File permissions 0o600, directory 0o700. Tombstone files for clear tracking. fcntl-based exclusive file locking.

key_functions.name: FilesystemStore.load
key_functions.summary: Reads YAML credential file. Refuses symlinks and group/world-readable files.

key_functions.name: FilesystemStore.save
key_functions.summary: Atomic write via temp file. Sets 0o600 permissions. Removes tombstone if present.

key_functions.name: FilesystemStore.clear
key_functions.summary: Deletes credential file and creates tombstone marker.

key_functions.name: FilesystemStore.is_cleared
key_functions.summary: Returns True if tombstone exists for this credential.

key_functions.name: FilesystemStore.list_users
key_functions.summary: Lists all users with saved credentials for a provider in a domain.

key_functions.name: FilesystemStore.lock
key_functions.summary: Context manager using fcntl.flock for exclusive access during refresh.

extension_points: Implement SecretStore protocol for alternative backends (database, cloud secrets manager, keyring)
lifecycle_notes: Segment names validated against [a-z0-9_]+ regex — no hyphens, spaces, or uppercase
documentation_hooks: How to implement a custom SecretStore
risks: fcntl is Linux/macOS only — not portable to Windows
